title: Pedagogy-driven Evaluation of Generative AI-powered Intelligent Tutoring Systems
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a core problem in the evaluation of intelligent tutoring systems (ITSs), especially those powered by generative AI and large language models: existing evaluation practices are fragmented, overly reliant on subjective judgments or generic NLP metrics, and fail to capture pedagogical quality. The authors argue that the field lacks unified, reliable, and scalable evaluation frameworks that can measure whether AI tutors truly support learning rather than merely producing fluent responses.

Rather than reporting an empirical intervention study, the paper reviews the state of the art in ITS evaluation across traditional self-report methods, NLG-based automated metrics, and pedagogy-oriented human or model-based assessments. It then proposes three research directions: unifying evaluation frameworks and benchmarks, measuring pedagogical guidance in tutor responses, and measuring active learning through conversation dynamics. The approach is grounded in learning science concepts such as metacognition, constructivism, and inquiry-based learning.

The context is broad and cross-domain, covering prior ITS work in math, language, writing, and science, with examples drawn from educational dialogue datasets and existing AI tutor systems. The paper concludes that progress in GenAI-powered tutoring depends on developing standardized taxonomies, robust benchmarks, and scalable automated metrics aligned with pedagogical principles. It emphasizes that such unification would improve comparability, transparency, and reliability in both research and real-world deployment.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/review-and-proposal paper, not an empirical evaluation study. It does not report a new quantitative design, causal identification strategy, or original outcome evidence, so it does not meet evidence criteria for higher tiers.
impact_tier_rationale: No intervention effect is tested or estimated, and no measurable learning impact is reported. The paper proposes evaluation directions and frameworks, so there is no demonstrated impact size to classify beyond red.

interventions.use_case: A review and evaluation framework paper focused on GenAI/LLM-powered intelligent tutoring systems, including dialogue-based AI tutors such as LearnLM and Khanmigo, with emphasis on how to evaluate their pedagogical responses and learning-science alignment.

A broad evaluation-focused analysis of classical and modern ITSs, including rule-based and deep-learning tutors such as AutoTutor, DeepTutor, and Writing Pal, and discussion of their evaluation methods and pedagogical capabilities.
